Article 13
(1) In order to provide services and protection to Women and Children from violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT as an integrated service center for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements from the Health Office, Education Office, Youth and Sports Office, Social Office, Cooperatives, SMEs and Manpower Office, Industry and Trade Office, Population and Civil Registration Office, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Office, Community and Village Empowerment Office, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Police Resort, Kulisusu Palace Customary Institution, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Higher Education Institutions.
(3) Further provisions regarding PPT shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Sixth Part
Principles of Service and Assistance

PROTECTION
OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is North Buton Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of North Buton Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Buton.
-4-
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of North Buton Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children in the womb who become victims of violence as well as children in conflict with the law.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
-5-
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization that provides assistance.
-6-
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Fourth Part
Form and Mechanism of Service

Article 22
Letter a What is meant by "fast" is immediate action taken without complications or simplified procedures. What is meant by "safe" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, not disturbed, and served with friendliness, respect and appreciation.
What is meant by "empathy" is actions of appreciating, respecting, caring, being friendly, and making happy that aim to please and calm the hearts of victims.
Letter b What is meant by "guarantee of confidentiality" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.
-22- Letter c What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people regardless of their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively adequate for the privileged.
Letter d What is meant by "no fees charged" is that service and assistance activities carried out by PPT are not charged to victims.

3.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes spiritual/religious counselling as part of victim assistance/services. Pasal 1 angka 20 defines “Pendampingan” as actions including “bimbingan rohani” (spiritual guidance). Pasal 16 huruf d lists an SPM performance indicator: “cakupan layanan bimbingan rohani ...” (coverage of spiritual guidance services) provided by trained spiritual guidance officers. Pasal 19(2) also states services are implemented by regional apparatus in fields including “mental dan spiritual.” These provisions are present in the retrieved English candidates (notably [3.8-3] for the definition and [3.8-25] for ‘mental and spiritual’), so a correct judge could conclude the policy provides for spiritual counselling. The judge’s ‘No’ appears to apply an overly narrow requirement of an explicitly named ‘service unit,’ which is not required by the indicator and is contradicted by the SPM/definition language.

Article 17
Forms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. Socialization activities of laws and regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of Women and Children; and

L GENERAL
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, therefore legal protection is needed to protect their self-respect and dignity as well as to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 280 paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, as well as the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right."
The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in North Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children Victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is carried out based on the principles of respect for human rights, -19- justice, non-discrimination and victim protection. The objectives of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are to a) prevent violence against women and children; b) eliminate all forms of violence and exploitation against women and children; c) protect and provide a sense of security for women and children; d) provide services to women and children victims of violence, reporters, and witnesses; and e) facilitate and mediate domestic disputes to realize the integrity of harmonious and prosperous households.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in North Buton Regency.

Article 13
(1) In order to provide services and protection to Women and Children from violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT as an integrated service center for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements from the Health Office, Education Office, Youth and Sports Office, Social Office, Cooperatives, SMEs and Manpower Office, Industry and Trade Office, Population and Civil Registration Office, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Office, Community and Village Empowerment Office, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Police Resort, Kulisusu Palace Customary Institution, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Higher Education Institutions.
(3) Further provisions regarding PPT shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7
Exploitation as referred to in Article 2 letter e is caused by: -8-
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

4.1.rationale: The original Indonesian policy does include information/education activities as primary prevention. Pasal 17 states prevention by PPT can be implemented through “kegiatan sosialisasi peraturan perundang-undangan kepada masyarakat yang berkaitan dengan perlindungan hak Perempuan dan Anak” (community socialization/outreach of laws/regulations related to protection of women’s and children’s rights) and training of PPT members. This matches the judge’s cited English snippet and supports a ‘Yes’ for information/education on VAW prevention. Therefore the pipeline prediction is consistent with the source text, and the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.
